value.body: Public relations and advertising careers cover creating campaigns, managing media and brand reputation, and planning where ads run. Work happens in agencies (creative, media, PR firms) and in-house in companies' marketing and corporate-communications teams.

items.label: Typical entry roles
items.value: Account executive, copy trainee, PR executive, media planner

items.label: Employers
items.value: Ad agencies, media agencies, PR firms, in-house brand teams

value.title: How you get in
value.body: No fixed exam. A degree in mass communication, journalism, marketing or a related field helps, but entry is mostly through internships and a portfolio of writing, design or campaign work.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry pay is often modest and hours can be long around campaign launches.
Digital and social media now make up a large part of the work.
Growth comes through a portfolio and client results more than formal qualifications.
